knowledge_point.title: Finding an Area by Transforming to a Type I Region

question.:question/problem:
Using the change of variables 

$$
u=x - 8 y,\,v=y,
$$

calculate the area of the finite region $D$ bounded by the curve $(x - 8 y)^{2}-(y)=0$ and the line $y=4.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The area of the required region is given by

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows: 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane to our region $D$ in the $xy$-plane.

To compute the required area, we will use the change of variables formula

$$
{∬}_{D}dxdy={∬}_{Δ}|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\text{ }dudv
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$  

Note that the changes of variables

$$
u=x - 8 y,\,v=y
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y) \\ v(x,y)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required area, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Substituting $x - 8 y=u$ and $y=v$ into the equation of the first curve, we get

$$
(x - 8 y)^{2}-(y)=0\,⟹\,u^{2}-v=0\,⟹\,v=u^{2}.
$$

while substituting $y=v$ into the equation of the second curve, we obtain

$$
v=4.
$$

To find the intersections of the curves in the $uv$-plane, we solve the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\{\begin{aligned}v=u^{2} \\ v=4\end{aligned}\right.\,⟹\,u=\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection points are $(\pm 2,4).$

Therefore, our domain in the $uv$-plane has the type I representation

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 2,\,u^{2}\le v\le 4\}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/repairs/2026-10-20-early-cohort/jobs/17592186129197/review-1-policy-2-6d8162cdaa407593/runtime/plots/0dbb08bd423ce416da196588.png)

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x}&\frac{∂u}{∂y}\\\frac{∂v}{∂x}&\frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{matrix}\right| \\ &=\left|\begin{matrix}1&-8\\0&1\end{matrix}\right| \\ &=1\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=(1)^{-1}=1.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$  In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Compute the required area.

We calculate the required area by performing the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_D dxdy &=\iint_Δ |\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,dudv \\ &=\iint_Δ |1|\,dudv \\ &=1\int_{-2}^{2}[\int_{u^{2}}^{4}dv]du \\ &=1\int_{-2}^{2}[v]_{u^{2}}^{4}du \\ &=1\int_{-2}^{2}(4)-(u^{2})du \\ &=1\int_{-2}^{2}(4 - u^{2})du \\ &=1[- \frac{u^{3}}{3} + 4 u]_{-2}^{2} \\ &=1(((8)+(- \frac{8}{3}))-((-8)+(\frac{8}{3}))) \\ &=1(\frac{32}{3}) \\ &=\frac{32}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $D$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$

Substituting $x - y=u$ and $y=v$ into the equation of the first curve, we get

$$
(x - y)^{2}-(y)=0\,⟹\,u^{2}-v=0\,⟹\,v=u^{2}.
$$

while substituting $y=v$ into the equation of the second curve, we obtain

$$
v=1.
$$

To find the intersections of the curves in the $uv$-plane, we solve the following system:

$$
\begin{aligned}\left\{\begin{aligned}v=u^{2} \\ v=1\end{aligned}\right.\,⟹\,u=\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection points are $(\pm 1,1).$

Therefore, our domain in the $uv$-plane has the type I representation

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,u^{2}\le v\le 1\}.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/repairs/2026-10-20-early-cohort/jobs/17592186129197/review-1-policy-2-6d8162cdaa407593/runtime/plots/6a07bea707d38e08e39bb3fb.png)

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =\left|\begin{matrix}\frac{∂u}{∂x}&\frac{∂u}{∂y}\\\frac{∂v}{∂x}&\frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{matrix}\right| \\ &=\left|\begin{matrix}1&-1\\0&1\end{matrix}\right| \\ &=1\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}=(1)^{-1}=1.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$  In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Compute the required area.

We calculate the required area by performing the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_D dxdy &=\iint_Δ |\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\,dudv \\ &=\iint_Δ |1|\,dudv \\ &=1\int_{-1}^{1}[\int_{u^{2}}^{1}dv]du \\ &=1\int_{-1}^{1}[v]_{u^{2}}^{1}du \\ &=1\int_{-1}^{1}(1)-(u^{2})du \\ &=1\int_{-1}^{1}(1 - u^{2})du \\ &=1[- \frac{u^{3}}{3} + u]_{-1}^{1} \\ &=1(((1)+(- \frac{1}{3}))-((-1)+(\frac{1}{3}))) \\ &=1(\frac{4}{3}) \\ &=\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
